newsitem.title: Bangladesh: Bangladesh fires central bank chief.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh fires central bank chief.

text.p: Bangladesh's central bank Governor, Khorshed Alam, was fired on Thursday for alleged irregularities and a lack of control over his subordinates, Finance Minister S.A.M.S. Kibria said.
"The Governor has been relieved of his contract on the basis of an inquiry report," he told a news conference.
"The inquiry found that the governor had no control over his subordinates. Also he was found lenient about irregularities," a finance ministry official said.
The inquiry was launched in September, two months after the new government of Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina took office, he said without giving details.

Officials said the inquiry followed allegations that a deputy governor of the Bangladesh Bank, the country's central bank, had issued licences to some eight non-banking financial institutions without prior approval of the governor or the finance ministry.
The deputy governor, Mahbubur Rahman, had been suspended earlier.
The inquiry report, one official said, implied that Alam overlooked his deputy's conduct. The report recommended tough legal action against the central bank officials involved in the irregularities.

Finance ministry officials said Alam, a retired bureaucrat who was appointed governor of the Bangladesh Bank nearly four years ago, was served with a notice on Wednesday to quit office. Alam's contract was due to expire on December 19.
Alam was immediately replaced by Lutfar Rahman Sarkar, a career banker and the chief executive of the Prime Bank, a leading private sector bank.
Alam was not immediately available for comment.
